en.title: Change One Character to Get a Smaller Non-Palindrome
en.description:
Given a lowercase palindrome, change exactly one character so that the result is not a palindrome, is strictly smaller than the original string, and is the lexicographically smallest among all valid results; if there is no solution, output IMPOSSIBLE.

This site uses a standard input/output protocol; missing numeric ranges are stated explicitly.
en.input: One line containing a lowercase palindrome of length 1..1000.
en.output: Output the valid string or the uppercase IMPOSSIBLE.
en.explanation: Example 1: change the b at index 3 to a, giving aaaabaaa. Example 2: changing the center still gives a palindrome, and the other a characters cannot be lowered, so IMPOSSIBLE. Example 3: changing the first character to a gives ab, which is better than ba.
hints: Change the first non-a character in the first half to a; if there is none, it is impossible. The common variant that changes the last character to b cannot be used, because this problem explicitly requires the string to become smaller.
